profile.name: Name
profile.passwordAskPlaceholder: Leave empty to be asked when connecting
profile.passwordHint: Passwords are saved as chosen in Settings › Security.
profile.keyPathTip: ~ stands for your home folder, so this is {path}
profile.keyHint: If the key has a passphrase, you will be asked in the terminal when connecting.
profile.keyMissing: There is no file at this path on this computer.
profile.notesPlaceholder: For example, what this session is for
profile.notesHint: Shown when you point at the session in the list, and found by the search.
profile.agentHint: Uses the keys loaded in the system SSH agent.
profile.telnetLoginHint: If set, the user name and password are typed at the server's login and password prompts; otherwise the server asks in the terminal. Passwords are saved as chosen in Settings › Security.
profile.refreshDevices: Refresh the list of serial ports
profile.noDevices: No serial ports found. Connect the adapter and refresh, or type the device name.
profile.serialHint: Most devices use 115200 8N1 without flow control. While the session is open, other programs cannot use the device.
profile.discardMessage: The changes to this session haven't been saved.
profile.invalidPort: Port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
profile.keepaliveHint: 0 turns keepalives off. The connection is considered lost after 3 unanswered keepalives.
profile.keepaliveHintTelnet: TCP keepalives; 0 turns them off. The connection is considered lost after 3 unanswered keepalives.
profile.autoReconnect: Reconnect automatically when the connection is lost
profile.autoReconnectSerial: Reconnect automatically when the device is disconnected
profile.commandGroupHint: The quick commands its tabs show first.
profile.autoLogHint: From each connection on; can also be started and stopped from the tab's menu.
profile.invalidKeepalive: The keepalive interval must be an integer between 0 and 3600
profile.autoHint: Tries the SSH agent's keys and ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_ecdsa and id_rsa, then keyboard-interactive or password, as ssh does.
profile.passwordAutoHint: Used if the server asks for a password. Passwords are saved as chosen in Settings › Security.
profile.jumpHostsHint: Connects through these sessions in order, like ProxyJump.
profile.jumpHostsHintTelnet: Connects through these SSH sessions in order, like ProxyJump; the last one connects to the Telnet server.
profile.missingProxyHint: The proxy this session uses is missing (its file may have been set aside), so the session doesn't connect until the file is restored or another proxy is chosen.
profile.proxyHint: Connects through this proxy. Proxies are managed in Settings.
profile.proxyViaJumpHost: With jump hosts, the first one ({name}) is reached through its own proxy: {proxy}.
profile.invalidBaudRate: The baud rate must be a positive integer
profile.forwardAgentHint: Lets programs on the server (git, ssh to further hosts) use the keys in your local agent. Anyone with root access on the server can use them too while you are connected.
profile.encodingHint: For servers and network devices that don't use UTF-8; also used for file names in SFTP and ZMODEM. Changes apply from the next connection.
profile.loginCommandsPlaceholder: One command per line, e.g. sudo -i
profile.loginCommandsHint: Typed into each new shell in order, each once the shell shows its prompt. Ctrl+C skips the rest.
profile.envHint: Sent before the shell starts. The server only accepts the ones its AcceptEnv setting allows (often LANG and LC_*).
profile.invalidEnvLine: Environment variables are written as NAME=value: "{line}"
profile.appearanceHint: Changes the terminal of this session only; anything left as is follows the settings.
profile.customBackgroundHint: For example red for production servers. The session's tabs show the color too.
profile.invalidFontSize: The font size must be an integer between {min} and {max}

sftp.downloadToFolderTitle: Choose a folder to download into

forwards.title: Port Forwarding
forwards.empty: No forwarding rules yet. Rules are saved with this session and can start automatically when it connects.
forwards.profileMissing: This session has been deleted, so its forwarding rules are no longer available.
forwards.notConnected: Rules can be started once connected.

explain.local: Connections to {bind} on this computer are forwarded through the server to {target}.
explain.remote: Connections to {bind} on the server are forwarded through this computer to {target}.
explain.dynamic: A SOCKS proxy at {bind} on this computer; applications using it connect through the server.

dialog.exposedLocal: Other computers on your network will be able to connect to this port.
dialog.exposedRemote: Servers only listen on non-loopback addresses when GatewayPorts is enabled.
dialog.invalidBindPort: The listening port must be an integer between 0 and 65535
dialog.invalidTarget: A destination host and a port between 1 and 65535 are required

forwards.quickConnection: Port forwarding rules are saved with a session. Save this connection as a session (tab menu) to use them.

importDialog.title: Import from SSH Config
importDialog.empty: No hosts found. Only Host entries without wildcards can be imported.
importDialog.hint: Jump hosts are imported along with the hosts that use them, and each ProxyCommand as a proxy. Port forwards are imported without auto-start.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Text from servers and the system, such as server messages and file dialogs, keeps its own language.
settings.textSizeHint: For the app's own text. The terminal's font size is set under Terminal.
settings.appFontHint: For the app's own text. Missing characters fall back to the default fonts. The terminal's font is set under Terminal.
settings.showStatusBarHint: Below the terminals: the connection, data sent and received, the terminal type, the terminal's size and the cursor's position.
settings.fontHint: Missing characters, such as Chinese, fall back to system fonts.
settings.screenReaderHint: Screen readers such as VoiceOver, Narrator and NVDA can read the terminal and announce new output. Turn it on only while you use one: terminals with a lot of output become slower.
settings.copyOnSelect: Copy text as soon as it is selected
settings.rightClickHint: Shift+right-click always shows the menu, also in programs that use the mouse.
settings.confirmMultilinePasteHint: Not asked when the shell supports bracketed paste, which inserts the lines without running them.
settings.optionAsMetaHint: Option+B, Option+F and similar shortcuts reach the shell, but Option no longer types special characters.
settings.followRemoteTitle: Show the title set by the shell
settings.followRemoteTitleHint: Otherwise tabs show the session name. Renamed tabs keep their new name.
settings.confirmClose: Ask before closing tabs and panes that are connected or running a program
settings.downloadDirectoryHint: Files downloaded from the file panel without choosing a place, and files received with sz, are saved here.
settings.editorDefault: The application the system opens the file with
settings.editorHint: Remote files opened in an editor are uploaded again each time you save them.
settings.proxiesHint: Sessions choose a proxy on the Connection page of their settings. Through jump hosts, only the first jump host uses its proxy.
settings.zmodemReceiveHint: Showing a file that happens to look like sz output, with cat for example, also starts a transfer: asking keeps it from saving anything you didn't want.
settings.logDefaultDirectory: Use the default folder (ZShellLogs in Documents)
settings.logFileNameHint: {session}, {host}, {user}, {date} and {time} are replaced; a number is added if the file exists.
settings.logTimestamps: Start each line with its time
settings.logAutoHint: Saved sessions are recorded automatically if set in the session. Any tab can start or stop logging from its menu.
settings.knownHostsHint: Shared with OpenSSH. A host's key is added when you accept it on the first connection, and checked on every connection after that.

protectionState.passwordRemembered: Encrypted with a master password, remembered in {store}.

settings.securityHint: Covers sessions, folders, proxies, quick commands and saved passwords. Settings and session logs are not encrypted.

enable.password: Lock ZShell with the login password
enable.polkit: Lock ZShell with the account password

appLock.hint: Covers the window until you unlock it; sessions keep running meanwhile. Lock now with {shortcut}.

appLock.idle: Lock when the computer has been idle for
appLock.onSystemLock: Lock when the computer sleeps, locks its screen or switches user

knownHosts.search: Search hosts, key types or fingerprints

setAside.title: Some data could not be read

setAside.notMoved: {name} was left as it is, and changes to what it holds aren't saved until ZShell can read it. Restart ZShell to try again.

saveFailed.quickCommands: The quick commands could not be saved, so your change was undone: {error}

sessionImport.title: Import Sessions
sessionImport.hint: Jump hosts and proxies are imported along with the sessions that use them, or matched to existing ones. Folders are merged by name.
sessionImport.autoForward: Forwards {rule} ({kind}) as soon as it connects
sessionImport.forwardAgent: Lets the server use your SSH agent's keys (agent forwarding)
sessionImport.brings: Also imports {names}, which it connects through
sessionImport.broughtBy: Imported with {names}, which connects through it
sessionImport.encrypted: The file is encrypted, with the saved passwords in it. Enter the passphrase it was exported with to open it; the passwords are imported with the sessions.

proxy.name: Name
proxy.socksHint: Host names are resolved by the proxy. Passwords are saved as chosen in Settings › Security.
proxy.httpHint: Uses the CONNECT method; the connection to the proxy itself is not encrypted. Passwords are saved as chosen in Settings › Security.
proxy.commandHint: Runs on this computer for each connection, like ProxyCommand: the connection goes through its standard input and output, and what it prints as errors appears in the terminal. %h, %p and %r stand for the host, port and user name, %% for %.
proxy.commandPasswordHint: The command cannot ask for passwords. To go through another SSH server that needs one, use jump hosts instead.

statusBar.label: Status bar
statusBar.traffic: Sent {sent} and received {received} on this connection.
statusBar.trafficScope: Counts terminal data only, not file transfers or port forwarding.
statusBar.termType: Terminal type sent to the server (TERM)
statusBar.serialLine: Baud rate, data bits, parity and stop bits

vault.title: ZShell Is Locked
vault.passwordPrompt: Enter the master password to open your sessions.
vault.rememberedFailed: The remembered key could not be used: {message}
vault.keyUnavailable: The key to your encrypted sessions could not be read from {store}.
vault.new: Your sessions could not be saved.
vault.unreadable: The file with your sessions could not be read.
vault.damaged: The file with your sessions is damaged or was changed, and cannot be opened.
vault.newer: Your sessions were saved by a newer version of ZShell. Update ZShell to open them.
vault.resetMessage: Resetting deletes the file with your sessions: every session, folder, proxy, quick command and saved password in it is lost for good. Settings and session logs are kept.

prompt.touchId: Use Touch ID or the login password to unlock.
prompt.password: Enter the login password to unlock.
prompt.polkit: Authenticate with the account password to unlock.

appLock.goneHint: ZShell can be unlocked without authenticating.

protection.title: Change Protection
protection.introSystem: Your sessions and saved passwords are encrypted, with the key in {store}: ZShell unlocks by itself, and copies of the files elsewhere can't be read. A master password protects them from anyone who can use your account too. You can change this later in Settings › Security.
protection.introNone: Your sessions and saved passwords are not encrypted, because {store} could not be used. Encrypt them with a master password, or change this later in Settings › Security.
protection.passwordDescription: Enter it each time ZShell starts; until then the sessions and passwords stay encrypted. If you forget it they cannot be recovered, so export your sessions to keep a copy.
protection.systemDescription: ZShell unlocks by itself when it starts. Protects the files if they are copied somewhere else, such as a backup or a synced folder. Other apps need your permission to read the key.
protection.systemDescriptionShared: ZShell unlocks by itself when it starts. Protects the files if they are copied somewhere else, such as a backup or a synced folder, but any program you run can read the key.
protection.systemUnavailable: Not available: {store} could not be reached on this computer.
protection.noneDescription: Sessions and passwords are saved as they are, in vault.json. Anyone who can read the data folder, or a copy of it, can read them.
protection.rememberHint: The key is also kept in {store} and ZShell unlocks by itself, so anyone who can use your account can open your sessions.

exportDialog.title: Export Sessions
exportDialog.message: All sessions, with their folders and proxies, are saved to a file you choose. Without the saved passwords the file is not encrypted: anyone who has it can read the addresses, user names, login commands and environment variables.
exportDialog.includePasswords: Include saved passwords, and encrypt the file
exportDialog.passphraseHint: The whole file is encrypted with it. It is needed to import the file, and cannot be recovered.
